package_info.package_manager: custom (delivered via spearphishing document, not a public package repository)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is designed as a stealthy backdoor, providing remote access, command execution, payload delivery, and data exfiltration. It employs advanced obfuscation and anti-analysis techniques, and is delivered via targeted spearphishing to compromise high-value targets in the aerospace and defense sector.

execution_context.file_location: malicious job description PDF or document

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Dropper code embedded in the document: upon opening, extracts and executes the primary backdoor payload.
malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (or macro, depending on document type)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the malicious document, the embedded code executes, extracting the backdoor payload from the document to disk and launching it as a new process, resulting in initial system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Documents should not contain embedded code that extracts and executes binaries, as this is a common technique for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal job description files are static and do not contain executable code or mechanisms to drop and run additional payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate self-extracting installers may use embedded code, but not in the context of standard office documents or job descriptions.
key_indicators: Executable payload embedded within document file
Automatic process creation upon document open
Extraction of binary to disk from document content

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated backdoor code: decrypts API names only when called, communicates with C2 over custom HTTP protocol, supports command execution, payload download, and data exfiltration.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the dropped backdoor binary is executed, it decrypts required API names at runtime, establishes outbound HTTP connections to a command-and-control server using a custom protocol, receives and executes attacker commands, downloads additional payloads, and exfiltrates sensitive data from the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: On-the-fly API decryption and use of a custom HTTP-based C2 protocol are advanced evasion techniques rarely seen in legitimate software, indicating intent to avoid detection and enable covert remote control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not obfuscate all API calls or establish persistent connections to unknown external servers for remote command execution and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or anti-tamper solutions may obfuscate APIs, but do not provide remote shell access or data exfiltration capabilities.
key_indicators: Multiple string encryption methods for API names and C2 URLs
Custom HTTP-based C2 protocol with non-standard request patterns
Remote command execution, payload download, and data exfiltration functionality

attack_chain.action: Target receives and opens a malicious job description document.
attack_chain.leads_to: Dropper code executes, installing the backdoor.

attack_chain.action: Dropper extracts and executes the primary backdoor payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor is now running on the victim system.

attack_chain.action: Backdoor establishes communication with the C2 server using a custom protocol over HTTP.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can issue commands, download payloads, and exfiltrate data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker performs reconnaissance, executes commands, downloads additional payloads, and exfiltrates sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control and data theft.

behavioral_signatures: Document files (PDF, DOCX) that drop and execute binaries upon opening
Processes spawned from document viewers that write and launch new executables
Backdoor binaries that decrypt API names only at runtime
Custom HTTP-based C2 communication with non-standard protocols
Remote command execution and payload download capabilities
file_indicators: Job description documents with embedded executables
Dropped binaries with heavy string/API obfuscation
Unusual temporary files created upon document open, especially in user profile or temp directories
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP traffic to unknown or suspicious domains using custom protocols
C2 communication patterns not matching standard HTTP requests, such as non-standard headers or payload formats
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for document files that spawn new processes or drop executables to disk. Use endpoint security tools to flag binaries exhibiting heavy string or API obfuscation. Inspect outbound HTTP traffic for custom protocol usage or connections to suspicious domains. Alert on any process spawned from a document viewer that attempts network communication, command execution, or creates new files in temporary directories.
